description: First analytic known-answer batch for the CPU spectral atmosphere reference pipeline. These are toy physics cases with closed-form expectations, not Earth clear-sky comparisons.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth and beam transmittance definitions.
reference.derivationSummary: Optical depth is the path integral of extinction, tau = integral sigma_t ds, and beam transmittance is T = exp(-tau). With vacuum extinction sigma_t = 0 over any finite path, tau = 0 and T = 1.

tau.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: tau = integral sigma_t ds; vacuum sigma_t = 0 over any finite path, so tau = 0.

transmittance.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T = exp(-tau); with tau = 0, T = exp(0) = 1.

expectations.independence: Closed-form invariant from the transmittance equation; no production helper or local numerical integration is needed.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth as a path integral over distance.
reference.derivationSummary: Optical depth integrates extinction over path length. A zero-length path has no measure, so tau = 0 even if the local extinction is nonzero; therefore T = exp(0) = 1.

tau.derivation: PBRT optical-depth path integral: tau = integral sigma_t ds; with path length 0 km, the integral is 0 even when sigma_t is nonzero.

transmittance.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T = exp(-tau); with tau = 0, T = 1.

expectations.independence: Closed-form zero-measure path integral; it does not depend on any integrator implementation.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.derivationSummary: For constant extinction over distance d, optical depth simplifies to tau = sigma_t * d and transmittance becomes T = exp(-sigma_t * d).

tau.derivation: PBRT homogeneous Beer-Lambert: tau = sigma_t * d = 0.2 / km * 3 km = 0.6.

transmittance.derivation: PBRT homogeneous Beer-Lambert: T = exp(-tau) = exp(-0.6) = 0.5488116360940264.

expectations.independence: The expected values are hand-derived closed-form literals from the equation, not computed by reference package code.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.derivationSummary: Optical depths over adjacent segments add, tau_ac = tau_ab + tau_bc. Because T = exp(-tau), the combined transmittance is multiplicative: T_ac = T_ab * T_bc.

tauAC.derivation: PBRT optical-depth additivity along the same ray: tau_ac = tau_ab + tau_bc = 0.2 + 0.4 = 0.6.

transmittanceAB.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T_ab = exp(-tau_ab) = exp(-0.2) = 0.8187307530779818.

transmittanceBC.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T_bc = exp(-tau_bc) = exp(-0.4) = 0.6703200460356393.

transmittanceAC.derivation: PBRT multiplicativity: T_ac = T_ab * T_bc = exp(-0.2) * exp(-0.4) = exp(-0.6) = 0.5488116360940264.

expectations.independence: This is an algebraic property of exponential transmittance over adjacent path segments.

expectations.quantity: empty view-path optical depth and transmittance output

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth as a path integral and T = exp(-tau).
reference.derivationSummary: With no transport segment, the path integral has zero measure. The local packet schema should still make the zero optical depth and unit transmittance explicit at path end.

assumptions.packetSchemaPolicy: empty sample-aligned arrays are present and pathEnd totals are explicit

sampleCount.derivation: Local packet schema for an empty path: no transport samples are emitted.

pathEndTauByWavelength.derivation: PBRT path integral over an empty segment: tau = 0 for each wavelength.

pathEndTransmittanceByWavelength.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T = exp(-tau); with tau = 0, T = 1 for each wavelength.

expectations.independence: The physics result follows from a zero-measure path integral; the explicit empty-output shape is a local API contract, not implementation behavior.

expectations.quantity: monotonic cumulative optical depth and transmittance over two homogeneous intervals

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth integral and exponential beam transmittance.
reference.derivationSummary: For nonnegative homogeneous extinction, cumulative optical depth increases with distance and transmittance decreases because T = exp(-tau).

checkpointDistancesKm.derivation: Two ordered intervals of 1.5 km each have cumulative checkpoints at 1.5 km and 3.0 km.

cumulativeTauByCheckpoint.derivation: PBRT homogeneous Beer-Lambert at each checkpoint: tau = 0.2 * 1.5 = 0.3, then tau = 0.2 * 3 = 0.6.

transmittanceByCheckpoint.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T = exp(-0.3) = 0.7408182206817179 and T = exp(-0.6) = 0.5488116360940264.

expectations.independence: The expected values are closed-form checkpoint literals from homogeneous Beer-Lambert transport, not generated by the integrator.

expectations.quantity: independent per-wavelength optical depth and transmittance

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Volume Scattering Processes
reference.locator: Medium coefficients and radiometric quantities may vary spectrally.
reference.derivationSummary: Once extinction is wavelength-indexed, Beer-Lambert optical depth and transmittance apply independently at each wavelength.

tauByWavelength.derivation: PBRT homogeneous Beer-Lambert per wavelength: tau = [0.1 * 3, 0.2 * 3] = [0.3, 0.6].

expectations.independence: The expected arrays are hand-derived literals from per-wavelength Beer-Lambert transport and prove the fixture does not collapse spectra to one scalar.

expectations.quantity: species optical depths sum into total optical depth

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Volume Scattering Processes
reference.locator: Attenuation combines absorption and out-scattering effects through extinction.
reference.derivationSummary: Independent extinction contributors add into total extinction. The local diagnostics preserve species contributions while the total optical depth drives T = exp(-tau_total).

rayleighTauByWavelength.derivation: Species optical depth for Rayleigh fixture: tau_R = 0.1 / km * 3 km = 0.3.

mieTauByWavelength.derivation: Species optical depth for Mie fixture: tau_M = 0.2 / km * 3 km = 0.6.

totalTauByWavelength.derivation: PBRT attenuation/extinction combination with local species diagnostics: tau_total = tau_R + tau_M = 0.3 + 0.6 = 0.9.

transmittanceByWavelength.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T = exp(-tau_total) = exp(-0.9) = 0.4065696597405991.

expectations.independence: The expected species and total values are hand-derived additive optical-depth literals with the species names acting only as local diagnostic labels.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Volume Scattering Processes
reference.locator: Absorption and scattering coefficients as rates per unit distance.
reference.derivationSummary: Physical extinction is the nonnegative attenuation rate from absorption and out-scattering. A negative coefficient is invalid model data and should be rejected instead of clamped into plausible transport output.

expectedError.derivation: PBRT volume-scattering process definitions treat extinction contributors as nonnegative rates per unit distance; local error policy requires naming the invalid species and wavelength.

expectations.independence: The oracle is the physical nonnegativity invariant plus local loud-failure policy, not any current clamping or validation implementation.

expectations.quantity: weighted optical-depth integration over sampled medium intervals

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth as a path integral of extinction over distance.
reference.derivationSummary: The stage receives sampled extinction values and interval weights from the path sampler. For a piecewise-constant sampled fixture, optical depth is the weighted sum sum_i sigma_t_i * ds_i, and transmittance is exp(-tau).

tauByWavelength.derivation: PBRT optical-depth path integral specialized to sampled piecewise-constant intervals: tau = 0.4 * 0.25 + 0.2 * 0.75 + 0.1 * 2 = 0.45.

transmittanceByWavelength.derivation: PBRT transmittance definition: T = exp(-tau) = exp(-0.45) = 0.6376281516217733.

expectations.independence: The expected weighted sum is hand-derived from the packet's interval weights and extinction values; it proves the stage must use distances, not sample count.

reference.title: Reference Code Design
reference.locator: Inputs, Units, and Model Interface sections for wavelength-indexed transport arrays.
reference.derivationSummary: The wavelength grid owns spectral array order. A coefficient array that does not align to wavelengthsNm has no unambiguous physical meaning and must fail instead of being broadcast, truncated, or padded.

assumptions.invalidReason: one coefficient value for two wavelengths

expectedError.derivation: Local spectral-array contract: one extinction coefficient cannot define two wavelength samples without an explicit interpolation or broadcast policy, and no such policy exists in this stage.

expectations.independence: The oracle is the public spectral-array alignment contract, not any current array-handling implementation.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Transmittance
reference.locator: Optical depth as a path integral over distance.
reference.derivationSummary: Optical-depth integration weights represent path distances ds. A negative or non-finite weight is not a physical distance and must be rejected by an independently runnable stage.

expectedError.derivation: PBRT optical-depth integral uses ds as path length. A negative sample weight would subtract optical depth and violate the distance-domain contract.

expectations.independence: The oracle is the physical meaning of integration weights as path distances plus the public independently-runnable stage contract.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Phase Functions
reference.locator: Isotropic phase function and phase normalization over solid angle.
reference.derivationSummary: A normalized isotropic phase function is constant over the sphere. Since the sphere has solid angle 4*pi sr, the constant value must be 1 / (4*pi), and its integral over the sphere is 1.

integralOverSphere.derivation: PBRT phase normalization: integral over sphere = p * 4 * pi = (1 / (4 * pi)) * 4 * pi = 1.

expectations.independence: The value is the normalized constant over the unit sphere and does not depend on implementation direction conventions.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Volume Scattering / Volume Scattering Processes
reference.locator: Section 11.1.4 In Scattering, source function and phase-function in-scattering integral.
reference.derivationSummary: PBRT expresses in-scattering as incident radiance integrated against a phase function and scattering/attenuation terms. The local reference design specializes that to one sample, one wavelength, one source term, and one midpoint step.

assumptions.sourceTerm: direct spectral irradiance already evaluated for the sample

spectralRadiance.derivation: PBRT in-scattering source function specialized by the reference design to one source/sample step: dL = T_view * beta_sca * phase * source * T_source * ds = 0.5 * 0.2 * 0.25 * 4 * 0.8 * 2 = 0.16.

expectations.independence: The expectation is a scalar product from the documented equation with deliberately simple factors.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Reflection Models / Diffuse Reflection
reference.locator: Section 9.2 Diffuse Reflection, Lambertian BRDF f = R / pi and hemispherical normalization.
reference.derivationSummary: PBRT gives the Lambertian diffuse BRDF as reflectance divided by pi so integrated reflectance equals R. The local surface model specializes that to direct irradiance: L = albedo * E * max(cosTheta, 0) / pi before view attenuation.

surfaceLeavingRadiance.derivation: PBRT diffuse reflection f = R / pi, specialized to direct irradiance: L = albedo * E * cosTheta / pi; albedo = 0 makes L = 0.

cameraVisibleSurfaceRadiance.derivation: PBRT transmittance is multiplicative along the view path; surfaceLeavingRadiance = 0 and viewTransmittance = 1, so camera-visible radiance remains 0.

expectations.independence: The zero result follows directly from the Lambertian equation's albedo factor.

reference.title: PBRT v4, Reflection Models / Diffuse Reflection
reference.locator: Section 9.2 Diffuse Reflection, Lambertian BRDF f = R / pi and hemispherical normalization.
reference.derivationSummary: PBRT gives the Lambertian diffuse BRDF as reflectance divided by pi so integrated reflectance equals R. The local surface model specializes that to direct irradiance: L = albedo * E * max(cosTheta, 0) / pi before view attenuation. With albedo 1, normal incidence, and E = pi, the result is 1.

surfaceLeavingRadiance.derivation: PBRT diffuse reflection f = R / pi, specialized to direct irradiance: L = albedo * E * cosTheta / pi = 1 * pi * 1 / pi = 1.

cameraVisibleSurfaceRadiance.derivation: PBRT transmittance is multiplicative along the view path; surfaceLeavingRadiance = 1 and viewTransmittance = 1, so camera-visible radiance is 1.

expectations.independence: The expected value is a closed-form Lambertian normalization case chosen so E / pi = 1.
